SM Rezaul Karim, Advocate with Md Abdur Razzak, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md Jashimuddin, Assistant Attorney-General and Shah Abdul Hatem, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For the State-Opposite-Party No.1.

full_judgment:
Md Nazrul Islam Talukder J: On an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused-petitioner, a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the impugned proceedings of Special Case No. 23 of 2007 arising out of ACC GR No. 25 of 2007 corresponding to Motijheel Police Station Case No. 140 dated 29-3-2007 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007, now pending before the Special Judge, Court No.3 Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. The accused-petitioner is a businessman who was elected Secretary-General of Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies (in short BAIRA) in the year 2004-2006 and 2006- 2007. The accused-petitioner was a veteran Freedom-Fighter who used to perform outstanding social activities to promote the cause for the distressed people. However, a tender notice at the instance of RAJUK was published in the Daily Ittefaq on 5-6-2004 for sale of numerous abandoned properties. In response to that tender notice, the petitioner submitted a bid to purchase the case property being House No.130, New Eskaton, Dhaka. The bid of the petitioner was adjudged to be the highest. Accordingly, the petitioner purchased the case property on alleged auction. 

 4. Any way, on 29-3-2007, an ejaharwas lodged with Motijheel Police Station, DMP, Dhaka by one Shafiul Alam, Assistant Director of Anti-Corruption Commission, Dhaka stating inter-alia, that from 2004-2006, the FIR named accused Mirza Abbas Uddin Ahmed, the then Minister for Housing and Public Works abusing his official position and in connivance with some civil servants manipulated the tender for sale of the abandoned properties in Gulshan, Banani, Dhanmondi, Elephant Road, Shantinagar, New Eskatan etc. for the benefit for himself and other accused and sold the same at a less price than the market price thereby causing a huge financial loss amounting to Tk. 127,64,19,059.26 to the public exchequer. Against this backdrop, a case under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 was initiated against the accused-petitioner and others. It may be mentioned here that the accused-petitioner was not named in the ejahar. 

 5. However, after the lodgment of the ejahar with the concerned police station, the Anti- Corruption Commission investigated the case and having found a prima-facie case, the investigating officer submitted charge-sheet against 13 accused including the petitioner under the relevant provisions of law on 20-9-2007. Although the petitioner is not named in the ejahar but he has been charge-sheeted along with others. It has been stated in the charge-sheet that the alleged criminal liabilities of the petitioner are that of the abetment in manipulating the tender for sale of the abandoned properties, which is punishable under sections 4091109 of the Penal Code. 

 6. Following submission of charge-sheet, the learned Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka took cognizance of the offences against the accused-petitioner under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004. Subsequently, the learned Special Judge, by an order dated 17-2- 2008, framed charge against the accused-petitioner and others under the aforesaid provisions of law. It may be mentioned that the accused-petitioner was an absconder at the time of framing charge against him. Under the circumstances, the petitioner was wanted in the trial Court. However, on 25-8-2008, the accused-petitioner appeared before the High Court Division with an application for anticipatory bail whereupon the High Court Division issued the Rule and enlarged the accused-petitioner on ad- interim anticipatory bail till disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 13081 of 2008 which was possibly filed by one of the co-accused. 

 7. As per latest propositions of law declared by the Apex Court, an accused cannot remain on anticipatory bail for an unlimited period. Anticipatory bail may be granted to an accused for a limited period or till filing of the charge-sheet whichever is appropriate in the circumstances of the case. After expiry of the period or filing of the charge-sheet, as the case may be, the accused must appear before the Court concerned and obtain fresh bail from the Court on the merit of the case. 

 9. It is on record that on 25-8-2009, at the time of issuance of the Rule, all further proceedings of Special Case No.23 of 2007 were stayed for a period of 1 (one) year or till disposal of Writ Petition Nos. 6869 of 2008, 7336 of 2008, 7190 of 2008 and 7229 of 2008 whichever is earlier. Subsequently, the order of stay was extended for a further period of 6(six) months or till disposal of the aforesaid writ petitions by an order dated 27-9-2010. 

 10. At the very outset, Mr. SM Rezaul Karim, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner, submits that at the time of filing of the instant application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioner was on pre-arrest bail granted by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14063 of 2008 on 25-8-2008 and, as such, the petitioner was not fugitive from justice at the time of moving the instant application before the High Court Division and this being the position, the instant application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is maintainable in the eye of law. He next submits that following the tender notice published in the Daily Ittefaq on 5-6-2004, the petitioner participated in the tender process and the bid of the petitioner being the highest one was accepted by the authority concerned and, as such, the petitioner is a bona fide purchaser for value and this being the state of affairs, the impugned proceedings should be quashed. He then submits that the bid money to the tune of Tk. 2,69,17 lakh quoted .by the petitioner was higher than the minimum price fixed by the price evaluation committee and in that view of the matter, it cannot be said by any stretch of imagination that the petitioner influenced the tender process in collaboration with other public servants and the allegation of abetment paddling against him is imaginary and unfounded and under the given context, the impugned proceedings should be quashed. He lastly submits that the facts disclosed in the charge-sheet having no tangible basis do not constitute any offence against the accused-petitioner and non-disclosure of any offence against the petitioner is a good ground for quashing the impugned proceedings. Learned advocate, in support of his submissions, has drawn our attention to the decisions taken in the cases of Abdul Quader vs State reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain, 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16, Murad Ali vs State, 22 DLR (WP) 158, Moklesur Rahman vs State, 35 DLR 72 and Sher Ali vs State, 46 DLR (AD) 67. 

 11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has also relied on some unreported decisions given in the cases of Mrs. Hasna Ahmed vs State in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14295 of 2008, Ahmed Akbar Sobhan alias Shah Alam, Chairman, Bashundhara Group vs State in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 16422 of2011, SM Anwar Hossain vs The State in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 26562 of 2009 with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 26563 of 2009 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 26562 of 2009, Ahmed Akbar Sobhan alias Shah Alam vs State in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 16423 of 20 11, Mehedi Hasan vs State in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9051 of 2011 but the learned Advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission informs us that Criminal Petitions For Leave to Appeal Nos. 292 of 2012, 293 of2012 and 514 of 2012 have been filed against the judgments passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 16422 of 2011, 16423 of 2011 and 9051 of 2011 respectively and they are awaiting hearing. 

 12. Per contra, Mr. Jashim Uddin, learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of State-opposite-party No.1, submits that though the petitioner is not named in FIR but admittedly, he was been charge-sheeted by the Anti-Corruption Commission and the case is virtually a bundle of facts which can only be thrashed out during the trial of the case and from this stand-point, the impugned proceedings initiated against the accused-petitioner and others should not be quashed. 

 13. On the other hand, Mr. AKM Fazlul Haque, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Anti-Corruption Commission, opposite-party No. 2, submits that the petitioner is not FIR named but after investigation, he has been charged-sheeted and his involvement in this case is a matter of evidence and trial and in view of the above facts and circumstances of the case, the prosecution case should not be quashed at this stage unless an opportunity of adducing evidence to prove the charge of abetment against the accused-petitioner is given. He next submits that it transpires that the tender process was manipulated to give illegal benefit to the beneficiaries including the petitioner and some public functionaries and this tender manipulation cannot be resolved in an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and in order to resolve the same, the accused-petitioner must face the trial of the case before the trial Court and in that view of the matter, the impugned proceedings should not be quashed, He then submits that admittedly the petitioner is a beneficiary of the illegal transaction and if the Rule is made absolute, other beneficiaries will get scot free and this will have demoralized effect upon the prosecution case and from this stand-point, the prosecution case should not be quashed. Mr. Haque further submits that considering the statements given by the witnesses, the investigating officer submitted charge-sheet against the accused-petitioner and a clear case of abetment has been disclosed against the accused-petitioner and accordingly the learned Special Judge rightly took cognizance and framed charge against the accused-petitioner and considering that aspect of the case, no exception can be taken thereto at this stage and under the given context, the impugned proceeding should not be quashed. He emphatically submits that the accused- petitioner obtained pre-arrest bail from the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous case No, 14063 of 2008 after framing charge against him by the learned Special Judge when he was wanted before the Court below and considering that aspect of the case, the accused-petitioner was not legally entitled to file an application for anticipatory bail and to obtain a pre-arrest bail from the High Court Division as he was wanted in the trial Court. He lastly submits that since the accused-petitioner did not approach this Court with clean hands for filling an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and since he is fugitive from justice, the application filed by the accused-petitioner under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is incompetent and not maintainable in the eye of law and, as such, the impugned proceedings should not be quashed. The learned Advocate for opposite-party No.2, in support of his contentions, has referred to the decisions settled in the cases of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mahmud Hossain, 61 DLR (AD) 17, Anti-Corruption Commission vs ARM Nazimullah Chowdhury, 62 DLR (AD) 225 and Anti-Corruption Commission vs Md Obaidul Karim, 15 BLC (AD) 159. 

 14. In view of the submissions and counter submissions advanced by the learned Advocates for the respective parties, a pertinent question arises as to whether the impugned proceedings should be quashed, To decide this issue, it will be necessary to see the extent of power, scope, principles and categories of cases in which High Court Division may invoke its extra-ordinary power and authority under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing a proceeding. 

 15. In the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs State, 28 DLR (AD) 38 where it has been spelt out that to bring a case within the purview of section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the purpose of quashing a proceeding, one of the following conditions must be fulfilled:- 

 (1) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on admitted facts no case stands against the accused, 

 (4) In a case where the allegation in the FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not constitute the offence alleged. 

 (5) The allegations against the accused although constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge. 

 16. Similar view, on the principle for quashing the proceeding, was subsequently, followed in the case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain, 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16. 

 18. In case of Sher Ali vs State reported in 46 DLR (AD) 67 wherein it has been decided; 

 19. Keeping in view the aforesaid proposition of law settled by the Apex Court, we have gone through the prosecution materials on record. It appears from the record of the case that the case properties which were sold on auction at the instance of the accused were under the disposal of the Management Board constituted under the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order, 1972 (President Order No.16 of 1972), and the Bangladesh Abandoned property (Buildings in the Urban Areas) Rules, 1972. As per Rules 9 and 10 of the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Buildings in the Urban Areas) Rules, 1972, the 'Management Board' constituted under Rule 9 of the above mentioned Rules is authorized by law to lease out or dispose of the abandoned properties by way of hire purchase system or by outright auction. For the sake of convenience of discussion, it will be profitable to quote Rules 9 and 10 of the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Buildings in the Urban Areas) Rules, 1972 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules only). 

 21. Pursuant to the above provisions of law, a Management Board, headed by Divisional Commissioner was constituted for control, Management and disposal of the case properties by a Notification No.SRO 77-Ain/90 dated 20-2-1990, which is evident from the charge-sheet. So, the management and disposal of the buildings, in question, were never put under the disposal of RAJUK. Accordingly, the RAJUK has no authority and jurisdiction to lease out or to dispose of the property either on hire-purchase system or by outright auction. We don't find any paper and document which may indicate that the government directed the Management Board constituted under the law to sell out the abandoned properties for the welfare of the people and the country as well. 

 22. From the facts and circumstances of the case, we hold that prima-facie, the FIR named accused Mirza Abbas Uddin Ahmed, the then Minister for Housing and Public Works abusing his official position and in connivance with other accused manipulated the tender for sale of the abandoned properties for benefit for himself other accused causing a huge financial loss to the public exchequer. 

 29. On going through the relevant provisions of law on abetment of offences, an abetment may be said to be committed by a person who, by his engagement or act or illegal omission, instigates any person to do a thing. In the instant case, we find that first of all, the petitioner participated in the tender for sale of the abandoned properties in question; secondly the petitioner is a beneficiary of the alleged illegal transaction; thirdly, the petitioner has an engagement in the alleged illegal transaction for purchasing the case property in his favour or otherwise in favour of BAIRA from the principal accused. From the aforesaid standpoint, we are of the view that a prima-facie allegation of abetment in manipulating the tender for sale of the abandoned properties has been disclosed against the accused- petitioner. 

 30. It has been contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that following the tender notice published in the Daily Ittefaq on 5-6-2004 for sale of the abandoned properties, the petitioner participated in the tender and his bid for purchase of the case property being the highest one was accepted by the authority and, as such, the petitioner being a bona fide purchaser for value cannot be held liable for the offences under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code. 

 31. In reply, learned Advocate for the Anti- Corruption Commission has contended that the FIR named accused Mirza Abbas Uddin Ahmed, the then Minister of the Housing and Public Works in connivance with other accused manipulated the tender for sale of the case properties and directed the RAJUK in a dishonest way to sell out the same on alleged auction for the benefit of his own and other beneficiaries. The submissions made by the learned Advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission have been emboldened by the charge-sheet submitted by the Anti-Corruption Commission. 

 32. Under the circumstances, the question arises whether the petitioner abetted the principal accused in manipulating the tender for sale of the abandoned properties; whether he abetted the principal accused in purchasing the case property; whether he purchased the case property in connivance with other accused; whether the petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for value. 

 33. It is now well-settled that whether the petitioner had any role in the illegal transaction or whether he abetted the principal accused in manipulating the tender for sale of the case properties and whether the petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for value are all disputed questions of fact which may be resolved on taking evidence by the trial Court. It is a settled principle of law that the disputed question of fact cannot be determined by this Court invoking its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Over and above, whether the allegations of abetment in manipulating the tender for sale of the case properties are true or false can only be gone into during the trial of the case. Moreover, the admissibility, relevance, propriety or sufficiency of materials collected by the prosecution are also matters for evidence and trial. 

 34. For instance, we may refer to the decision taken in the case of Hossain Mohammed Ershad vs State reported in 45 DLR (AD) 48, where in it has been held:- 

 "In a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure the High Court Division should not be drawn to an enquiry as to the truth or otherwise of the facts which are not in the prosecution case. Whether HM Ershad as the President of the State allowed the application for the questioned allotment on the ground of compassion after considering that the applicant's earlier auction bid was illegally rejected by the RAJUK, whether his wife had any personal involvement in the alleged transaction or the subsequent transfer to the JPL was a mere corporate venture of the company itself, whether MM Rahmatullah merely followed the orders of the president and acted within the rules of the RAJUK, and whether other co- accused had any role in the transaction or whether they abetted the principal offenders are involved questions and can only be decided on evidence after juxtaposing the prosecution case with the defence of the accused. This is not a case of no offence disclosed prima facie. There is thus no legal impediment for the proceeding to continue. There is no cause or occasion for an interference for the ends of justice." 

 35. In this connection, we may refer to another decision in the case of Dr. M Faruq vs State 16 BLD (AD) (1996) 51, wherein it has been settled:- 

 36. In the case of Moudud Ahmed vs State, 16 BLD (AD) 27 = 48 DLR (AD) 42 wherein it has been laid down:- 

 37. We have stated earlier that the impugned proceeding may be quashed in view of the principles set out in the decisions settled in the cases of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs State, 28 DLR (AD) 38, Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain, 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16, Sher Ali vs State, 46 DLR (AD) 67. 

 38. Considering the case-decisions referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, a question arises whether the ingredients for quashing the impugned proceedings are available in the instant case. 

 39. We have stated earlier that the allegations of abetment against the accused-petitioner in manipulating the tender for sale of the abandoned properties have been prima-facie found true in the investigation report submitted by the investigating officer duly empowered by the Anti-Corruption Commission. It is an indisputable fact that the petitioner participated in the tender for sale of the abandoned properties in question and he is a beneficiary of the alleged illegal transaction. Furthermore, the petitioner has an engagement in the alleged illegal transaction for purchasing the case property in his favour or otherwise in favour of his organization from the principal accused. The aforesaid elements certainly attract the allegations of abetment in manipulating the tender for sale of the abandoned properties. Moreover, the abetment is such an offence which may be inferred from the conducts of the accused and circumstances of the case. It may be proved either by oral and documentary evidence or by circumstantial evidence. Under the circumstances, we have no hesitation in holding that there is no ingredients of quashing the impugned proceedings in the instant case as the prosecution materials indicate prima-facie offence of abetment against the accused-petitioner who prima-facie abetted the principal accused in manipulating the tender for sale of the abandoned properties. Accordingly, the decision in the case of Murad Ali vs State, 22 DLR (WP) 158 adverted to by the learned Advocate for the petitioner is not applicable to the present case. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has also banked upon the decision in the case of Moklesur Rahman vs State, 35 DLR 72 but the fact of the reported case is quite distinguishable from the present case and, as such, the same is also not applicable to the instant case. For the obvious reasons and observations made above for arriving at a decision in this Rule, we are not at one with the views expressed by other Benches of this Court in above-mentioned unreported criminal miscellaneous cases. 

 41. Before parting with the case, we like to observe that following the submissions of the police report, the learned Special Judge took cognizance of the offence against the accused-petitioner and thereafter, on 17-2-2008, the learned Special Judge also framed charge against the accused-petitioner under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code. After framing charge, the accused-petitioner came up with an application for anticipatory bail before the High Court Division and obtained anticipatory bail on 25- 8-2008 though he was wanted before the Court below. After obtaining anticipatory bail, the accused-petitioner approached this Court with an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure with a view to quashing the impugned proceedings and obtained the Rule and stay in respect of the impugned proceedings. 

 42. It is a settled principle of law that after filing of the police report there is no scope for granting anticipatory bail or pre-arrest bail to the accused of the case. In the instant case, the learned Special Judge framed charge against the accused-petitioner on 17-2-2008 following submission of charge-sheet submitted against him on 20-9-2007 and accordingly, he was very much wanted in the Court below; but he was an absconder in the trial Court. Since the petitioner was in abscondence from the proceedings, the requirements of law as contemplated by section 6(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 were complied with before commencement of the trial of the case. Eventually, inspite of the above gazette notification and commencement of the trial of the case, the accused-petitioner remained in abscondence from the proceedings. In such a situation, he had no locus-standi to prefer an application for anticipatory bail before the High Court Division on 25-8-2009. Since the accused-petitioner was an absconder and he was fugitive from the justice, he was not entitled to prefer any application for anticipatory bail before the High Court Division after framing charge against him and accordingly, the order of anticipatory bail even if granted by the High Court Division is illegal in the eye of law as per settled decisions of the Apex Court. Despite our earnest query, the learned Advocate for the petitioner could not produce any scrap of paper before us in order to show that after obtaining anticipatory bail, the petitioner voluntarily surrendered before the concerned Court below and obtained regular bail there from. Considering that aspect of the case, the accused- petitioner was not entitled to prefer an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before this Court on 25-8-2009 and in that view of matter, the Rule issued under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure is quite incompetent and not sustainable in the eye of law. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has pointed out that the accused-petitioner could not surrender before the court below even after submission of the police report and framing charge against him due to turbulent and turmoil situation arising out of emergency in the country; but the fact remains that the Emergency Power was withdrawn through জরুরী ক্ষমতা (রহিতকরন) অধ্যাদেশ-২০০৮ by the Hon'ble President of the Country by publishing a Gazette Notification dated 15-12-2008 with effect from 17- 12-2008. Surprisingly enough, even after withdrawal of the Emergency Power, the accused-petitioner has not surrendered before the Court below and strangely remained silent about the surrender before the Court below till today. Under the circumstances, the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner in the matter of surrender does not carry any conviction. 

 43. It is now well settled that after submission of the police report, there is no scope for anticipatory bailor pre-arrest bail as has been held in the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury reported in 51 DLR (AD) 242, wherein it has been observed in paragraph No. 43 :- 

 "Anticipatory bail should be granted by the High Court Division for a limited period or till filing of the charge-sheet whichever is appropriate in the circumstances of the case. After expiry of the period or filing of the charge-sheet, as the case may be, the accused must appear before the court concerned and obtain fresh bail from the Court on the merit of the case". 

 44. But curiously, the accused-petitioner approached this Court with an application for anticipatory bail after framing charge and obtained anticipatory bail ignoring the aforesaid decision of the Apex Court though he was fugitive from justice. In this context, we may refer to another decision in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mahmud Hossain, 61 DLR (AD)17, wherein it was laid down in paragraph No. 13 :- 

 In that decisions it was also observed in paragraph No. 16 "Even in our jurisdiction this principle is always adhered to and was never deviated from, as because this convention or principle has been a norm maintained in our criminal jurisprudence to affect the audience or appearance of the accused in reply to any process of the Court. This has become very much a practice and procedure in our Criminal Jurisprudence that a person in obedience to a process of the Court must surrender before the Court and challenge the alleged action against him. In the instant case, the petitioner having not surrendered to the process of the Court could not file any application or put his grievance before a Court of law, far less before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. Thus, in the absence of any surrender before the process of law, the Court of law is incompetent to issue any order or stay any process at its behest and if done so, that would be illegal and without jurisdiction and, as such, this petition is not maintainable." 

 45. In view of above facts and circumstances of the case and propositions of law, we are of the view that in the absence of surrender before the process of the Court, the application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the accused-petitioner is incompetent and not maintainable in the eye of law. 

 46. From the foregoing discussions and regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case and the propositions of law discussed above, we are led to hold that the impugned proceedings initiated against the accused-petitioner under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code cannot be quashed and that the same are maintainable in the eye of law. 

 47. Having considered all the aspects of the case, we do not find any merit in this Rule. Accordingly, the Rule fails. 

 50. The accused-petitioner is directed to surrender before the concerned Court below within 7 days from the date of receipt of this judgment by the learned Special Judge who shall be at liberty to consider the application for bail on the merit of the case if the accused-petitioner surrenders before Court below and prays for regular bail. 

 51. The learned Trial Judge is directed to proceed with the trial of the case in accordance with law.
